candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: Treating God as a universal best explanation supplies no discriminating explanatory power because it is indistinguishable from magic or invented alternatives.
candidates.attributionBasis: The passage occurs within Dillahunty's uninterrupted opening turn and uses his characteristic first-person reference to universe-creating pixies.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This challenges the explanatory foundation of the cumulative theistic case by arguing that an explanation compatible with virtually every outcome confirms nothing distinctive.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: The earlier pro position that God is the best causal explanation for features of reality.

candidates.contextSummary: After discussing fallible inference, Dillahunty argues that merely invoking God can answer almost any question and therefore cannot distinguish theism from magic.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: Religious claims require a method that reliably selects one hypothesis over competing religions rather than reproducing mutually incompatible conclusions.
candidates.attributionBasis: The sustained first-person account of former Southern Baptist belief appears inside Dillahunty's explicitly continuous opening presentation.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This establishes the skeptical standard applied throughout the debate and directly contests whether the Christian cumulative case uniquely warrants its conclusion.
candidates.contextSummary: Dillahunty traces religions through human testimony and error, applies skepticism to his former faith, and demands a consistently discriminating epistemic methodology.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: A God who wants people to know him should generate observable expectations, so pervasive reasonable nonbelief is substantial disconfirming evidence for that God model.
candidates.attributionBasis: Dillahunty explicitly introduces his own two arguments and describes his skeptical position during the same uninterrupted speaking turn.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Divine hiddenness is one of the debate's named central issues and bears directly on whether the Christian God's alleged aims fit the observed world.
candidates.contextSummary: He frames God models as prediction-generating hypotheses and argues that absent expected signs count against a clarity-seeking God without deductively disproving one.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: Competing and internally divided revelations undermine Christianity because believers identify errors in rival traditions without applying the same skepticism to their own.
candidates.attributionBasis: The passage continues Dillahunty's announced second argument and includes a detailed first-person account of seeking divine guidance and receiving silence.
candidates.loadBearingReason: Inconsistent revelation is a named central route in the motion and challenges both Christianity's distinctiveness and the claimed clarity of divine communication.
candidates.contextSummary: Dillahunty links reasonable nonbelief to disagreements among denominations and religions, then contrasts claimed revelation with his sincere but unanswered search for guidance.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: Even spectacular apparent miracles would not uniquely establish God because advanced intelligence, deception, or unknown mechanisms could produce the same observations.
candidates.attributionBasis: The speaker identifies his own work as a magician and mentalist within Dillahunty's uninterrupted autobiographical opening presentation.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This explains the skeptic's evidential threshold and blocks an inference from astonishing unexplained events directly to the specifically Christian supernatural explanation.
candidates.contextSummary: Considering what might convince him, Dillahunty distinguishes extraordinary phenomena from their cause and uses stage magic to illustrate how confidently observers can misattribute effects.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: No available method reliably points to any God, while a truth-seeking Christian God should communicate more clearly than through an ancient, altered, disputed story.
candidates.attributionBasis: The first-person skeptical conclusion closes Dillahunty's turn immediately before the moderator announces Hunter's rebuttal.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This synthesizes the methodological, hiddenness, and revelation objections into a direct comparative case for skepticism over Christian theism.
candidates.contextSummary: Dillahunty concludes that consistent scrutiny has not identified a reliable route to God and argues that a clarity-valuing Jesus could reveal himself directly.

candidates.speaker: Braxton Hunter
candidates.proposition: Dillahunty's stated evidential threshold is unrealistically skeptical because even conspicuous, specifically theistic public phenomena would not warrant belief for him.
candidates.attributionBasis: The moderator explicitly introduces Hunter before this rebuttal, and the speaker repeatedly addresses Matt by name from the opposing position.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move contests the reasonableness of the con side's governing evidential standard and seeks to prevent that standard from controlling the audience's assessment.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Dillahunty's earlier claim that unexplained spectacular phenomena would not uniquely establish that a God caused them.

candidates.contextSummary: Hunter characterizes Dillahunty as unconvinced by imagined multilingual lunar writing or an ocean parting in Jesus's name and urges listeners to reject that standard.

candidates.speaker: Braxton Hunter
candidates.proposition: General theistic arguments can legitimately support God before resurrection evidence identifies that deity as the Christian God.
candidates.attributionBasis: This remains within Hunter's introduced rebuttal turn and explicitly refers to his own first two arguments and resurrection case.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move defends the cumulative architecture connecting generic theism to the debate's specifically Christian conclusion rather than requiring every premise to be uniquely Christian.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Dillahunty's earlier objection that arguments shared with other religions do not establish the specifically Christian God.

candidates.contextSummary: Hunter separates his case into generic monotheistic arguments and a resurrection argument, claiming their conjunction supplies the Christian identification.

candidates.speaker: Braxton Hunter
candidates.proposition: Divine hiddenness is weakened because substantial evidence for God already exists and God seeks freely chosen trust and loyalty rather than mere compelled intellectual assent.
candidates.attributionBasis: The passage is part of Hunter's continuous rebuttal and explicitly names Matt's hiddenness argument before answering it from a theistic perspective.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This directly answers a named central objection by offering both an empirical denial of severe hiddenness and a purpose-based explanation for limited divine manifestation.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Dillahunty's earlier argument that widespread sincere nonbelief disconfirms a God who wants people to know that he exists.

candidates.contextSummary: Hunter cites arguments, science, history, philosophy, and experience as available evidence, then says relational freedom may justify God not appearing publicly and irresistibly.

candidates.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
candidates.proposition: Libertarian freedom is unsupported and conflicts with a creator who knowingly selects a complete universe and whose plan and prophecies fix how events unfold.
candidates.attributionBasis: The passage begins after Hunter's rebuttal ends and contains Dillahunty's explicit first-person identification as a compatibilist responding to Hunter.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The move attacks both the phenomenon supposedly explained by God and the coherence of combining libertarian agency with classical Christian foreknowledge and providence.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Hunter's earlier position that libertarian free choices exist and are best explained by an immaterial divine mind.

candidates.contextSummary: Dillahunty denies evidence that anyone could have done otherwise and argues that divine foreknowledge, creation, providential planning, and prophecy are incompatible with libertarian choice.
